title: Build a decision tree from scratch
brief: Write Gini and entropy, a fast split search with running sums, then grow, predict with, and prune a tree.
hints: Sort each feature once with numpy.argsort, then sweep a running left-side sum (and sum of squares, for mse) as you move one point at a time from right to left. Skip a candidate threshold when it falls between two equal feature values, since no split is possible there.

For gini and entropy, use numpy.bincount(y) to get class counts, divide by the total to get proportions, and apply the formulas directly. Guard entropy against log(0) by masking out zero-count classes before taking the log.

grow_tree should stop recursing when the node is already pure (impurity at or below a small tolerance), when max_depth is reached, when there are too few samples to make two leaves of size min_samples_leaf, or when best_split finds no split with positive gain.

cost_complexity_prune is a bottom-up recursion: at each internal node, compare the cost of collapsing it to a leaf (n_samples * impurity + alpha) against the summed cost of keeping its two (already-pruned) children, and keep whichever is cheaper.
